chapter.p: THE PROPHECY OF NEPHI, THE SON OF HELAMAN

p.i: God warns the Nephites that He will punish them in His anger to their complete destruction unless they repent of their wickedness. God punishes the Nephites; they repent and turn to Him. Samuel, a Lamanite, prophesies to the Nephites.

chapter.li: LEChapter7 Verse1 In the 69th year of the judges’ rule over the Nephites, Nephi, the son of Helaman, returned from the north to Zarahemla. VerseEnd Verse2 He taught God’s word and prophesied many things to the people there. VerseEnd Verse3 But they rejected everything he said, so he left them and returned to his native land. VerseEnd Verse4 He found the people had become awful and corrupt. There were Gaddianton robbers filling the judgment seats. They had seized control of the land. They disregarded God’s commandments. They defied Him and acted abusively to people. VerseEnd Verse5 They condemned the righteous because of their righteousness. They let the guilty and wicked go unpunished because of their money. They were given control over the government to do anything they wanted, and they wanted money and adoration from the public, which allowed them to commit adultery, steal, kill, and indulge themselves. VerseEnd Verse6 It had only taken a few years for this widespread iniquity to be welcomed by the Nephites. When Nephi saw it, it broke his heart. He lamented: VerseEnd Verse7 I wish I could have lived during the time when my forefather Nephi first came from the land of Jerusalem; I wish I could have felt joy with him in the promised land. At that time, his people were easy to persuade, firm in keeping God’s commandments, and slow to want to commit iniquity. And they were quick to listen and obey the Lord’s words. VerseEnd Verse8 Indeed, if my days could have been in those days, my soul would have rejoiced in the righteousness of my fellow Nephites. VerseEnd Verse9 But I was born at this time and live at a time that fills me with sorrow because of the wickedness of my fellow Nephites. VerseEnd

Verse10 Now Nephi was on a tower in his garden, next to the highway leading to the main marketplace of the city of Zarahemla. As Nephi prayed on the garden tower next to his garden gate by the highway, VerseEnd Verse11 some men were passing by and saw him lamenting to God. They ran and told the people what they had seen. And a big group of people went to learn the reason for him lamenting over the people’s wickedness. VerseEnd

Verse12 When Nephi got up, he saw a crowd had gathered. VerseEnd Verse13 He asked them: Why have 2PP you come here? 2PP You want me to tell 2PP you about 2PP your iniquities? VerseEnd Verse14 Is it because I’ve gotten on my tower in order to lament to God as I mourn over 2PP your terrible iniquities? VerseEnd Verse15 Is it because of my mourning and lamentation 2PP you’ve come here and act surprised? Indeed, 2PP you should be surprised! 2PP You should be surprised by how 2PP you’ve surrendered to the accuser and given him complete control over 2PP your hearts. VerseEnd Verse16 Why have 2PP you surrendered to the lies of someone who wants to drag 2PP your souls down to everlasting misery and endless suffering? VerseEnd

Verse17 O repent, repent! Why are 2PP you determined to die? Turn back, turn back to the Lord who is God! Do 2PP you know why He’s abandoned 2PP you? VerseEnd Verse18 It’s because 2PP you’ve hardened 2PP your hearts. Indeed, 2PP you ignore the Good Shepherd’s voice. 2PP You’ve made Him angry at 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse19 Therefore instead of gathering 2PP you, He’ll exterminate 2PP you and feed dogs and scavengers with 2PP your carcasses, unless 2PP you repent. VerseEnd Verse20 How could 2PP you turn 2PP your back on God in the very moment He saved 2PP you? VerseEnd Verse21 It’s because 2PP you want wealth, to be envied for 2PP your gold and silver. 2PP You only value wealth and worldly things of no real value, and to get it 2PP you’re willing to murder, rob, steal, and tell lies about 2PP your neighbor and do every kind of evil. VerseEnd Verse22 Because of this, 2PP you’re headed for misery and calamity unless 2PP you repent. If 2PP you don’t repent, this great city and all the other great cities throughout our land will be lost, leaving 2PP you no place to live. Because the Lord won’t protect 2PP you against 2PP your enemies, as He’s done until now. VerseEnd Verse23 This is what the Lord says: I won’t support the wicked with My protection for any one more than another, but I protect only those who repent of their sins and obey Me.

So now my friends 2PP you’ll find it will be better for the Lamanites than for 2PP you unless 2PP you repent. VerseEnd Verse24 They’re more righteous than 2PP you, since they haven’t sinned against the great knowledge given to 2PP you. Therefore the Lord will be merciful to them. He’ll lengthen out their days and increase their offspring, while 2PP you’ll be completely destroyed unless 2PP you repent. VerseEnd Verse25 Woe to 2PP you because 2PP you welcome the great abomination founded by Gaddianton which 2PP you’ve embraced by joining that gang. VerseEnd Verse26 2PP You’re doomed to misery and calamity because 2PP you’re full of pride, which has corrupted 2PP you as a result of 2PP your great wealth. VerseEnd Verse27 Woe to 2PP you because 2PP you are wicked and abominable, VerseEnd Verse28 and unless 2PP you repent, 2PP you will perish; and 2PP you’ll lose all 2PP your lands, and 2PP you’ll be annihilated. VerseEnd Verse29 Now I’m giving this warning not from myself, but from God. God sent me to warn 2PP you, otherwise I wouldn’t know this is 2PP your doom. VerseEnd

LEChapter8 Verse1 When Nephi finished these words, there were judges who belonged to the secret society of Gaddianton who were angry and shouted to the people: Why don’t 2PP you arrest this man and bring him to trial, so he can be condemned for the crime he’s committed? VerseEnd Verse2 Why are 2PP you looking at and listening to this man, when he’s denouncing 2PP you people and our laws? VerseEnd Verse3 They said this because Nephi had spoken to them about how corrupt their laws were. Indeed, Nephi said many things that can’t be written here. But he didn’t say anything contrary to God’s commandments. VerseEnd Verse4 And those judges were angry with him because he was blunt about their secret works of darkness. Nevertheless, they didn’t dare arrest him, since they were afraid the people might not support them. VerseEnd Verse5 Therefore they appealed to the people: Why are 2PP you letting this man ridicule us? He’s threatening this whole nation with destruction, and he claims we’ll lose our great cities, and we won’t have any place left to live. VerseEnd Verse6 Now we know this is impossible. Because we are powerful and our cities are great; therefore our enemies can’t prevail against us. VerseEnd

Verse7 So they inflamed the people until they argued over Nephi, some denounced him and some objected saying: Leave this man alone, because he’s a good man; and the things he said are certain to happen unless we repent. VerseEnd Verse8 All the judgments of God he said are coming are going to come to us, since we can see he’s right about our many iniquities. He also knows everything that will happen to us because he identified our iniquities. VerseEnd Verse9 Indeed, if he wasn’t a prophet, he wouldn’t have testified about these things. VerseEnd

Verse10 The people who wanted to kill Nephi were intimidated, so they didn’t arrest him. Therefore he began to prophesy again, seeing he had some support, so that the rest of them were intimidated. VerseEnd Verse11 Therefore he was inspired to say to them: My friends, haven’t 2PP you read God gave power to the man Moses to divide the water of the Red Sea? And the water parted to one side and the other, so our ancestor Israelites walked through on dry ground. Then the water fell upon the Egyptian armies, swallowing them up. VerseEnd

Verse12 Now if God guided this man, then why do 2PP you argue among yourselves and refuse to accept He guided me so I know about His coming judgments upon 2PP you unless 2PP you repent? VerseEnd Verse13 2PP You not only reject my words, but 2PP you also reject all the words of our forefathers, and also the words of Moses, who clearly had great power given to him; and he testified about Christ’s coming. VerseEnd Verse14 Indeed, didn’t he testify the Son of God was to come? He lifted up the brass serpent in the wilderness, as a sign that He who was to come would be lifted up. VerseEnd Verse15 Just as all those who looked on that serpent would live, similarly, all those who look to the Son of God with faith, having a repentant spirit, will live, and even receive life which is eternal. VerseEnd Verse16 Now Moses wasn’t the only one who testified of these things, but all the holy prophets from his day back to the days of Abraham did as well. VerseEnd Verse17 And Abraham saw His coming and was filled with gladness and rejoiced. VerseEnd Verse18 I tell 2PP you Abraham wasn’t the only one who knew of these things, there were many before Abraham’s time who were called by the Order of God, according to the Holy Order of His Son, and this was to show to the people thousands of years before His coming that redemption was available to them. VerseEnd Verse19 Now I want 2PP you to know that ever since Abraham’s time there have been many prophets who have testified about this. The prophet Zenos testified boldly — and for that he was killed — VerseEnd Verse20 and Zenoch, Ezaias, Isaiah, and Jeremiah as well. Jeremiah was the same prophet who testified about Jerusalem’s destruction. We’ve learned Jerusalem was destroyed according to Jeremiah’s words. So why won’t the Son of God come according to his prophecy? VerseEnd Verse21 Will 2PP you argue Jerusalem wasn’t destroyed? Will 2PP you say Zedekiah’s sons weren’t killed, all except for Muloch? Indeed, can’t 2PP you see Zedekiah’s descendants are here and they were led from the land of Jerusalem? But this isn’t everything. VerseEnd Verse22 Our father Lehi was forced out of Jerusalem because he testified of these things. Nephi and nearly all our forefathers down to today have all testified about it as well. They’ve testified of Christ’s coming and have looked forward rejoicing at His coming day. VerseEnd Verse23 And He is God; and He is with them, and He revealed Himself to them, and He redeemed them. They worshiped Him because of what’s to happen. VerseEnd

Verse24 Now seeing as 2PP you know this and will lie if 2PP you deny it, which is 2PP your sin because 2PP you’ve rejected all these things, despite the clear evidence given to 2PP you. Indeed, 2PP you’ve been given evidence both in heaven and on earth as a witness that they’re true. VerseEnd Verse25 But 2PP you’ve rejected the truth and rebelled against 2PP your holy God. Right now, instead of storing up for yourselves treasures in heaven — where nothing can destroy and where nothing unclean can enter — 2PP you’ve earned condemnation for yourselves on judgment day. VerseEnd Verse26 Indeed, right now 2PP you’re ripening — because of 2PP your murders, sexual immorality, and wickedness — for everlasting destruction. Unless 2PP you repent, it’s coming soon. VerseEnd Verse27 It’s at 2PP your doorstep. Go to the judgment seat and investigate what’s happened there; 2PP your judge has been murdered, and he’s lying in his blood. His brother, whose goal is to sit in the judgment seat, has murdered him. VerseEnd Verse28 They both belong to 2PP your secret society, founded by Gaddianton and the Evil One, whose goal is to destroy people’s souls. VerseEnd

LEChapter9 Verse1 Now when Nephi said this, five men who were there ran to the judgment seat. They said to each other as they were going: VerseEnd Verse2 Now we’ll know for certain whether this man is a prophet and whether God has commanded him to prophesy such astonishing things to us. We don’t believe that He has; and we don’t believe he’s a prophet. However, if what he’s said about the chief judge is true, that he’s dead, then we’ll believe the other things he’s said are true. VerseEnd Verse3 And they ran quickly to the judgment seat where the chief judge was on the ground lying in his blood. VerseEnd Verse4 When they saw this, they were shocked, so much so they fainted, since they hadn’t believed the things Nephi had said about the chief judge. VerseEnd Verse5 But when they saw this, they believed; and they feared all the judgments Nephi predicted. So they trembled with fear and fainted. VerseEnd

Verse6 Now the judge was stabbed by his brother, who then escaped using a disguise. As soon as the judge was murdered, the servants ran and told the people, yelling a murder had happened. VerseEnd Verse7 And the people gathered at the judgment seat. To their astonishment, they saw the five men who had fainted. VerseEnd Verse8 Now the people didn’t know anything about the crowd gathered at Nephi’s garden. Therefore they said to each other: These men are the ones who have murdered the judge; and God has struck them down to prevent their escape. VerseEnd

Verse9 So they took them, tied them up, and threw them into prison. And it was announced the judge was killed and the murderers were captured and were being held in prison. VerseEnd Verse10 The next day, the people assembled to mourn and fast at the burial of the murdered highest and chief judge. VerseEnd Verse11 The judges who were at Nephi’s garden and overheard him also attended the burial. VerseEnd

Verse12 And they asked the others: Where are the five who were sent to ask about the chief judge, to find out whether he was dead? And they answered: We don’t know about the five 2PP you sent, but we have five murderers now in our prison. VerseEnd Verse13 Then the judges asked to see them, and they were brought out. Then they recognized the five who had been sent. The judges questioned them about the matter. And they explained: VerseEnd Verse14 We ran to the judgment seat. When we saw everything just like Nephi described, we were shocked and we fainted. When we had recovered from our shock, they threw us in prison. VerseEnd Verse15 Now as to this man’s murder, we don’t know who did it. We only know this much: we ran and came just as 2PP you asked, and he was dead just as Nephi had said. VerseEnd

Verse16 Now the judges described the matter in detail to the people and accused Nephi, saying: We know Nephi must have conspired with someone to kill the judge; then he would be able to tell it to us, so he could convert us to his faith, so he could raise himself to be a great man, chosen by God and a prophet. VerseEnd Verse17 Now we’ll expose this man, and get his confession and reveal the judge’s true murderer. VerseEnd Verse18 The five were set free on the day of the burial. However, they rebuked the judges for speaking against Nephi, confronting them one after another, countering their arguments and proving them wrong. VerseEnd

Verse19 Nevertheless, they had Nephi arrested, tied up, and brought before the crowd who had gathered. And they began to question him in various ways trying to get him to contradict himself, so they could condemn him to death, VerseEnd Verse20 asking him: 2PSI You’re part of a conspiracy, an accomplice! Who’s 2PSI your associate that committed this murder? Tell us and admit 2PSI your guilt! And they also offered: Here’s some money! We’ll let 2PSI you live if 2PSI you tell us and admit 2PSI you’ve made an agreement with someone. VerseEnd Verse21 But Nephi responded: 2PP You fools, 2PP you unconverted in heart, 2PP you blind and stubborn people, do 2PP you have any idea how long the Lord 2PP your God will let 2PP you continue in 2PP your sinful ways? VerseEnd Verse22 2PP You ought to begin weeping and wailing over the destruction now coming for 2PP you, unless 2PP you repent. VerseEnd Verse23 2PP You say I conspired with a man to murder Seezoram, our chief judge. But I told 2PP you because I wanted 2PP you to know it had happened. 2PP You need to realize I know of all 2PP your wickedness and abominations. VerseEnd Verse24 Because I’ve exposed 2PP your wickedness, 2PP you accuse me of conspiring with a man to commit this murder. Because I showed 2PP you this sign, 2PP you’re angry and want to have me killed. VerseEnd

Verse25 Now I’ll show 2PP you another sign, and we’ll see if 2PP you want to kill me for this one as well. VerseEnd Verse26 I tell 2PP you: Go to the house of Seantum, who is Seezoram’s brother, and ask him: VerseEnd Verse27 Has Nephi, the so-called prophet, who prophesies so much evil about us, conspired with 2PSF you, and as part of this conspiracy have 2PSF you murdered 2PSF your brother Seezoram? VerseEnd Verse28 And he’ll tell 2PP you: No. VerseEnd Verse29 Then ask him: Did 2PSF you murder 2PSF your brother? VerseEnd Verse30 And he’ll stand there afraid, not knowing what to say. And he’ll deny he did it; and he’ll pretend to be surprised. Nevertheless, he’ll tell 2PP you he’s innocent. VerseEnd Verse31 But when 2PP you examine him, 2PP you’ll find blood on the bottom part of his cloak. VerseEnd Verse32 When 2PP you see this, 2PP you should ask: Where does this blood come from? Isn’t this 2PSF your brother’s blood? VerseEnd Verse33 And then he’ll shake with fear and his face will lose its color and look as pale as death. VerseEnd Verse34 Then 2PP you should say: Because of how afraid and pale 2PSF you look, we know 2PSF you’re guilty. VerseEnd Verse35 Then he’ll be even more afraid; and he’ll confess and no longer deny he committed this murder. VerseEnd Verse36 And then he’ll tell 2PP you that I, Nephi couldn’t know anything about it unless it was revealed to me by God’s power. Then 2PP you’ll know I’m honest and I’m sent to 2PP you from God. VerseEnd

Verse37 And they went and did just as Nephi had said to them. The things he predicted were true; because just as he described, Seantum denied, and then like he predicted, he confessed. VerseEnd Verse38 He was exposed as the actual murderer, so the five were vindicated, and Nephi proven innocent. VerseEnd Verse39 Some of the Nephites believed in Nephi’s words. Others believed because of the testimony of the five, who had been converted while they were in prison. VerseEnd Verse40 Some of the people said Nephi was a prophet. VerseEnd Verse41 And others said: He’s a god; because if he wasn’t a god, he couldn’t know about everything. Indeed, he’s told us the thoughts of our hearts, and he’s foretold things to us as well, and he’s even identified the murderer of our chief judge. VerseEnd

LEChapter10 Verse1 This resulted in an argument among the people, so they split up, going away and leaving Nephi standing alone. VerseEnd Verse2 Nephi went to return to his own house, pondering about what the Lord had shown him. VerseEnd Verse3 As he was pondering this, regretting the Nephites’ wickedness, their secret works of darkness, murders, robberies, and all their iniquities; reviewing these in his heart, a voice spoke to him, saying: VerseEnd Verse4 2PSI You are blessed, Nephi, because of the things 2PSI you’ve done. I’ve seen how 2PSI you’ve tirelessly declared the word I gave 2PSI you to this people. 2PSI You haven’t been afraid of them and haven’t tried to save 2PSI your own life, but have tried to learn My will and to keep My commandments. VerseEnd Verse5 Now because 2PSI you’ve done this so tirelessly, I’ll bless 2PSI you forever. And I’ll make 2PSI you powerful in word and deed, in faith and works, so that all things will happen to 2PSI you as 2PSI you ask, since 2PSI you won’t ask anything contrary to My will. VerseEnd Verse6 2PSI You are Nephi and I Am God. I declare this to 2PSI you in front of My angels as witnesses: 2PSF You are given power over this people and will strike the earth with famine, disease, and destruction in response to this people’s wickedness. VerseEnd Verse7 Indeed, I give 2PSF you power that whatever 2PSF you seal on earth will be sealed in heaven, and whatever 2PSF you set loose on earth will be set loose in heaven, and so 2PSF you will hold this power over this people. VerseEnd Verse8 And so if 2PSF you say to this temple: Split in two! — it will happen. VerseEnd Verse9 And if 2PSF you say to this mountain: Fall down and be leveled! — it will happen. VerseEnd Verse10 And if 2PSF you say for God to afflict this people, it will happen. VerseEnd Verse11 Now I command 2PSF you to go and warn these people that the Lord God, the All-Powerful One, decrees: Unless 2PP you repent, 2PP you will be afflicted and destroyed. VerseEnd

Verse12 Now when the Lord said this to Nephi, he stopped, turned around, and didn’t go to his house, but warned the many people spread across the land about the Lord’s words promising to destroy them if they didn’t repent. VerseEnd Verse13 Now despite the great miracle of Nephi telling them about the murder of the chief judge, they hardened their hearts and refused to pay any attention to the Lord’s words. VerseEnd Verse14 But Nephi declared to them the Lord’s word, saying: Unless 2PP you repent, the Lord says 2PP you will be afflicted and destroyed. VerseEnd Verse15 When Nephi delivered this message, they still hardened their hearts and ignored what he said. The people mocked him and attempted to seize him so they could throw him in prison. VerseEnd Verse16 But God’s power was with him, and they were unable to grab him and put him in prison because he was taken by the Spirit and carried away from them. VerseEnd

Verse17 And so he went forth in the Spirit from gathering to gathering declaring God’s word, until all of them heard it directly or indirectly. VerseEnd Verse18 But they refused to respond to his warning. But there began to be heated arguments, so much so that they fought among themselves and began to kill each other with the sword. VerseEnd Verse19 And so ended the 71st year of the judges’ rule over the Nephites. VerseEnd
